question: What does *(p + 2) evaluate to, and why?
options: 1, because pointers always start counting from 1
3, because p points to arr[0], so p + 2 points to arr[2], and dereferencing gives its value
A compile-time error, since arrays cannot be assigned to pointers
explanation: An array name decays to a pointer to its first element, so p == &arr[0]. p + 2 points to arr[2] (value 3), and *(p + 2) dereferences that address to get 3 — equivalent to arr[2].
